SIMULATIONS & OBSERVATIONS

What each curve is made of.

The 19 simulations differ in numerical method, code, resolution and purpose; the 82 observational sources differ in survey, facility and what they measure. Those differences are a large part of why curves disagree, so they are recorded here.

Simulations

Grouped by how the gas is evolved. Dates are the year the flagship paper was posted to arXiv. Set-up, physics and purpose follow the flagship abstracts; code names, box sizes and team names that an abstract does not state come from background knowledge and are not all checked against the full papers, so check the linked papers before quoting them. The "In sim-highline" line is computed from the data.

SPH

Smoothed particle hydrodynamics follows the gas with Lagrangian particles whose properties are smoothed over neighbours. It conserves mass by construction and follows collapse well; shocks and fluid instabilities need care. Codes here: Gadget-3 family, MP-Gadget, Gasoline, ChaNGa, SWIFT (SPHENIX).

ASTRID 2021 (overview paper)

Code
MP-Gadget · Springel 2005 (GADGET-2, the base of the Gadget-3 family)
Method
Smoothed particle hydrodynamics with tree-PM gravity (MP-Gadget, a Gadget-3 descendant)
Set-up
Periodic box of 250 Mpc/h with 2×5500³ particles, run from z=99 to z=3; galaxies resolved in haloes above 2×10⁹ M☉.
Physics
Inhomogeneous H and He reionization, baryon relative velocities, massive neutrinos, supernova and AGN feedback, black-hole mergers driven by dynamical friction.
Purpose
A large high-redshift galaxy sample that can be compared with future survey data.
Team
ASTRID (Bird, Ni and collaborators)
Papers
Bird et al. 2021, overview · Ni et al. 2021, supermassive black holes

BlueTides 2015 (overview paper)

Code
MP-Gadget · Springel 2005 (GADGET-2, the base of the Gadget-3 family)
Method
Pressure-entropy formulation of SPH with tree-PM gravity (MP-Gadget)
Set-up
Periodic box of 400 Mpc/h with 2×7040³ particles, run on Blue Waters from z=99 to z=8.
Physics
Gas cooling, star formation including molecular hydrogen, black-hole growth, stellar and AGN feedback.
Purpose
The first galaxies, quasars and their contribution to reionization at z>8, in the largest hydrodynamic volume at that redshift when it was run.
Team
BlueTides (Feng, Di Matteo and collaborators)
Papers
Feng et al. 2015, overview · Huang et al. 2018, black-hole galaxy relations

COLIBRE 2025 (overview paper)

Code
SWIFT · Schaller et al. 2024 (SWIFT)
Method
Smoothed particle hydrodynamics with the SPHENIX scheme in the SWIFT code
Set-up
Periodic boxes up to 400 cMpc at three resolutions (gas particle mass about 10⁷, 10⁶ and 10⁵ M☉); dark matter supersampled by a factor 4 so that dark matter and baryon particle masses are similar.
Physics
Multiphase ISM without a pressure floor, non-equilibrium H and He, dust model with three grain species and two sizes, pre-supernova and supernova feedback, thermal AGN feedback (plus hybrid jet runs).
Purpose
A new galaxy formation model with a cold, dusty multiphase ISM, calibrated to the z≈0 galaxy stellar mass function and stellar mass-size relation.
Team
COLIBRE project (Schaye and collaborators)
Papers
Schaye et al. 2025, overview · Chaikin et al. 2025, GSMF and SFR evolution

EAGLE 2014 (overview paper)

Code
Gadget-3 (modified) · Springel 2005 (GADGET-2, the base of the Gadget-3 family)
Method
Smoothed particle hydrodynamics in a modified Gadget-3 code
Set-up
Periodic boxes of 25, 50 and 100 cMpc; Ref-L100N1504 is the flagship run, Recal-L025N0752 the recalibrated high-resolution run.
Physics
Thermal-energy feedback from massive stars and AGN without turning off cooling, so winds develop without a prescribed speed or mass loading.
Purpose
Follow galaxies and black holes in representative volumes, with feedback calibrated to the z≈0 galaxy stellar mass function and galaxy sizes.
Team
Virgo Consortium (EAGLE project)
Data
Halo and galaxy catalogues and particle data are public (McAlpine et al. 2015; EAGLE team 2017).
Papers
Schaye et al. 2014, overview · Crain et al. 2015, calibration · McAlpine et al. 2015, catalogue release

FLAMINGO 2023 (overview paper)

Code
SWIFT · Schaller et al. 2024 (SWIFT)
Method
Smoothed particle hydrodynamics with the SPHENIX scheme in the SWIFT code
Set-up
Boxes up to 1.0 and 2.8 Gpc at several resolutions (the runs used here include L1_m8, L1_m9, L1_m10 and L2p8_m9), plus model and cosmology variations.

FLARES 2020 (overview paper)

Code
Gadget-3 (EAGLE model) · Springel 2005 (GADGET-2, the base of the Gadget-3 family)
Method
Smoothed particle hydrodynamics with the EAGLE (AGNdT9) model
Set-up
Zoom simulations of 40 regions of different overdensity selected from a (3.2 cGpc)³ parent volume, combined with a weighting scheme that makes composite distribution functions representative of the parent volume.
Physics
The EAGLE galaxy formation model.
Purpose
High-redshift galaxy formation in the epoch of reionisation, including its dependence on environment, with a dynamic range beyond periodic boxes.
Team
FLARES project (First Light And Reionisation Epoch Simulations; Lovell and collaborators)
Papers

Magneticum Pathfinder 2025 (overview paper; papers using the runs go back to at least 2016)

Code
Gadget-3 (modified) · Springel 2005 (GADGET-2, the base of the Gadget-3 family)
Method
Smoothed particle hydrodynamics in a modified Gadget-3 code
Set-up
A ladder of boxes from about 18 to 2688 Mpc/h (Box4 to Box0) at several resolutions (mr, hr, uhr).
Physics
Cooling, star formation, metal enrichment, black-hole growth and feedback; tuned to the hot gas content of galaxy clusters.
Purpose
Cover the largest range of volumes and resolutions of any suite, tuned on the hot gas of clusters instead of the stellar mass function, and test how many scaling relations come out self-consistently.
Team
Magneticum Pathfinder (Dolag and collaborators)
Data
Scaling-relation tables are released by the authors (ingested by sim-highline).
Papers
Dolag et al. 2025, Encyclopedia Magneticum · Teklu et al. 2015, angular momentum and morphology

NIHAO zoom suite 2015 (NIHAO I)

Code
Gasoline2 · Wadsley et al. 2017 (Gasoline2)
Method
Smoothed particle hydrodynamics (Gasoline with an improved SPH implementation)
Set-up
About 100 cosmological zoom-in simulations (88 main haloes in the relation tables used here) from dwarf to Milky Way mass, an unbiased sample of merger histories, concentrations and spins.
Physics
The same star-formation and stellar-feedback treatment for every halo; later papers add black holes.
Purpose
Reproduce the observed inefficiency of galaxy formation across cosmic time with one fixed model, and study galaxy scaling relations at galaxy scales.
Team
NIHAO project (Wang, Dutton, Stinson, Macciò and collaborators)
Papers
Wang et al. 2015, NIHAO I · Dutton et al. 2016, NIHAO XII (scaling relations) · Blank et al. 2019, NIHAO XXII (black holes)

Romulus25 2016 (Romulus overview paper)

Code
ChaNGa · Menon et al. 2015 (ChaNGa)
Method
Tree plus smoothed particle hydrodynamics (ChaNGa, descended from Gasoline)
Set-up
Periodic box of 25 Mpc.
Physics
Supermassive black-hole formation, dynamics (sinking) and accretion of rotationally supported gas; star-formation and feedback parameters optimized against z=0 scaling relations.

Model black-hole formation, orbital decay and accretion in a cosmological volume to study co-evolution with galaxies.
Team
Romulus (Tremmel and collaborators)
Papers
Tremmel et al. 2016, Romulus · Ricarte et al. 2019, black-hole galaxy co-evolution

moving mesh

AREPO solves the equations on a Voronoi mesh whose cells move with the flow, combining Galilean-invariant finite-volume accuracy with the adaptivity of particles.

Illustris 2014 (overview papers)

Code
AREPO · Springel 2010 (AREPO)
Method
Moving Voronoi mesh (finite-volume hydrodynamics on a mesh that follows the flow)
Set-up
Illustris-1: periodic box of 106.5 Mpc with 2×1820³ resolution elements; dark-matter mass resolution 6.26×10⁶ M☉, baryonic 1.26×10⁶ M☉.
Physics
Primordial and metal-line cooling, star formation, stellar and AGN feedback, with a kinetic wind model.
Purpose
Simulate the coevolution of dark and visible matter, with a galaxy population in good agreement with many observed properties.
Team
Illustris Project (Vogelsberger, Genel and collaborators)
Papers
Vogelsberger et al. 2014, overview · Genel et al. 2014, galaxy populations

THESAN-1 2021 (overview paper)

Code
AREPO-RT · Kannan et al. 2019 (AREPO-RT)
Method
Moving Voronoi mesh with radiation-magnetohydrodynamics (AREPO-RT)
Set-up
Periodic box of 95.5 cMpc; flagship dark-matter and baryon masses 3.1×10⁶ and 5.8×10⁵ M☉; softening 2.2 ckpc, cells down to 10 pc at z=5.5.
Physics
Radiation transport coupled to the Illustris-TNG-like galaxy formation model; models the IGM during reionization.
Purpose
Model the large-scale statistics of the IGM during reionization together with the resolved properties of the galaxies that cause it.
Team
THESAN project (Kannan, Garaldi, Smith and collaborators)
Data
Public data release (Garaldi et al. 2023).
Papers
Kannan et al. 2021, overview · Garaldi et al. 2023, public data release

THESAN-zoom 2025 (overview paper)

Code
AREPO-RT · Kannan et al. 2019 (AREPO-RT)
Method
Moving Voronoi mesh with radiation hydrodynamics (AREPO-RT), zoom-in
Set-up
Zoom-ins of 14 high-redshift (z>3) galaxies selected from THESAN, with halo masses of 10⁸ to 10¹³ M☉ at z=3; best baryonic mass 142 M☉ and softening 17 cpc; 60 simulations including variations.
Physics
Multi-phase ISM with stellar feedback, radiation fields, dust and non-equilibrium thermochemistry; patchy reionization imported from the parent THESAN box.

High-resolution high-redshift galaxy formation with a detailed ISM model inside a realistic reionization background.

THESAN-ZOOM project (Kannan and collaborators)

meshless

GIZMO's meshless finite-mass (MFM) method uses particles as cell centres with a Riemann-solver flux between them, keeping mass conservation and improving shock and mixing treatment over classical SPH.

FIRE-2 2017 (FIRE-2 paper (FIRE-1 in 2013))

Code
GIZMO · Hopkins 2015 (GIZMO)
Method
Meshless finite-mass (MFM) hydrodynamics in GIZMO
Set-up
Zoom-in simulations of individual galaxies and their surroundings over a wide range of masses; the high-redshift sample used here is from Ma et al. 2018 (z≥5).
Physics
Multi-phase ISM, star formation, and stellar feedback from supernovae, stellar winds and radiation, with FIRE-2 numerical updates.
Purpose
Explore how stellar feedback shapes cosmological galaxy formation, with an emphasis on numerics versus physics.
Team
Feedback In Realistic Environments (FIRE) project
Papers
Hopkins et al. 2017, FIRE-2 · Ma et al. 2018, galaxies at z≥5

AMR

Adaptive mesh refinement (RAMSES) uses an Eulerian grid that is refined where the mass or the local Jeans length demands it, which resolves dense gas well and handles shocks and instabilities.

Horizon-AGN 2014 (overview paper)

Code
RAMSES · Teyssier 2002 (RAMSES)
Method
Adaptive mesh refinement (Eulerian grid refined where the mass or Jeans length requires it)
Set-up
Periodic box of 100 Mpc/h (about 142 cMpc); more than 150,000 galaxies per time step at 1.2<z<1.8.
Physics
Gas cooling, star formation, supernova and AGN feedback, black-hole growth.
Purpose
A large-volume simulation with AGN feedback to study galaxy morphology and colours, and the alignment of galaxies with the cosmic web.
Team
Horizon project (Dubois, Kaviraj and collaborators)
Papers
Dubois et al. 2014, overview · Kaviraj et al. 2017, galaxy properties over cosmic time · Volonteri et al. 2016, black holes

NewHorizon 2020 (overview paper)

Code
RAMSES · Teyssier 2002 (RAMSES)
Method
Adaptive mesh refinement
Set-up
A zoom-in region of about (16 Mpc)³ (a 10 Mpc-radius sphere) inside the Horizon-AGN box; resolution up to 34 pc within galaxies.
Physics
Multi-phase ISM, clumpy star formation, supernova and AGN feedback.
Purpose
Combine statistical power and high resolution: a zoom region larger than a single-halo zoom, embedded in a larger box, that resolves the internal dynamics of galaxies.

NewHorizon project (Dubois and collaborators)

Code
RAMSES-RT · Rosdahl et al. 2013 (RAMSES-RT)
Method
Adaptive mesh refinement with on-the-fly radiative transfer
Set-up
Periodic volumes of 5 and 10 cMpc in the first paper, and a 20 cMpc volume (SPHINX20); resolution about 10 pc; haloes resolved down to the atomic cooling limit.

Known metadata issues

Some observational records come from a machine-readable compilation whose stored citation can name a different paper than the label (flagged above as "check"); four such upstream citations were corrected in v0.6.0 and the original is kept with the record. 0 remaining mismatches found by the automatic check:

What is not here yet

A search of the simulation literature (specialised dwarf-galaxy suites such as LYRA and EDGE, zoom suites such as Auriga and APOSTLE, reionization suites, cluster suites, and the 2026 COLIBRE papers) is in docs/literature-candidates.md in the repository; entries are marked ingested, queued or skipped (with the reason) in data/literature-backlog.json.
